Setting up Atoms

Written against Obsidian 1.12.7 and BRAT 2.2.0.

Three parts. Get it installed, get capture onto your phone, then wire it into Claude or ChatGPT. The first part is the only one that is fiddly, and it is fiddly once.

1 · Install 2 · Capture 3 · Ask

1 · Install

Atoms runs inside Obsidian, so Obsidian comes first. If you already use it, start at step three. The whole thing takes about five minutes, and you can do it on a computer or on your phone — the menus are the same in both.

Get Obsidian

Download Obsidian. It is free, and it is a notes app where your files live on your device as plain text, not locked inside someone else's cloud.

Make a vault

A vault is just a folder that Obsidian watches. On first launch Obsidian asks what you want to do — choose Create new vault, give it a name, pick where it lives, and click Create. If Obsidian is already open, the vault switcher is the icon at the bottom of the left sidebar.

This is the one step with no shortcut: a folder only becomes a vault when Obsidian is told to treat it as one.

Turn on community plugins

A new vault starts in Restricted Mode, which blocks every plugin. Nothing can be installed until you leave it, and it is not obvious that you are in it.

Open Settings (the gear, bottom left) → Community plugins. Past the wall of security warnings there is one button: Turn on community plugins.

The pane changes once you do. Now it offers Browse and tells you that you have 0 plugins installed.

Install BRAT

Atoms is not in Obsidian's plugin directory yet, so it is installed through BRAT, a plugin whose whole job is installing other plugins from GitHub and keeping them current.

Hit Browse, search BRAT, and install the one called BRAT by TfTHacker. Enable it if it does not enable itself.

Point BRAT at Atoms

Open Settings → BRAT and press Add beta plugin, the button under Beta plugin list. On a computer the command palette does the same thing: Ctrl/Cmd + P, then BRAT: Plugins: Add a beta plugin for testing. In the box that appears, paste exactly:

taihartman/obsidian-atoms

The field's own example shows a full GitHub address, and that form works too — owner/repository is simply less to type. Then open the version dropdown, which starts on Select a version, and choose Latest version. Ignore the optional GitHub token, leave Enable after installing the plugin ticked, and press Add plugin.

BRAT downloads Atoms and switches it on for you. There is no separate step to enable it. If it somehow arrives switched off, it is under Settings → Community plugins → Installed plugins.

Check it worked

Open Settings → Atoms. If you see a version number at the top, you are done with the hard part.

Same screen is where you add your own Anthropic API key, or start a trial and let us handle the key. 14 days free, then $6/month. Cancel anytime. Card required for trial.

Staying up to date

Atoms ships often, and BRAT already handles it: Auto-update plugins at startup is on by default under Settings → BRAT, so new versions arrive the next time Obsidian starts. There is nothing to switch on — just know that is where it lives. If you would rather decide for yourself, turn it off and run BRAT's Check for updates by hand.

2 · Capture

Atoms only sorts what you actually wrote down, so capture has to be faster than the thought. The rule is one line, no filing, no deciding — you dump it, and Atoms works out later what it was.

Anywhere you can type into your daily note, you can capture: a top-level bullet like - ordered the wrong lens again is all a capture is. The phone Shortcut just makes that fast enough to use while walking.

iPhone and iPad

The plugin can install the Shortcut for you. Open Settings → Atoms → Capture and tap Install Capture Atom. That opens the shared Shortcut; Shortcuts still asks you to confirm before adding it.

Then put it somewhere you will actually reach: add it to your Home Screen, assign it to the Action Button, or set it as a Back Tap under Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap. A capture you have to go looking for is a capture you will not make.

Running it asks whether you want to type or dictate, then writes one timestamped line into Atoms System/Inbox.md. Next time Obsidian opens, each line moves into the daily note for the date it was captured. Nothing is deleted, and captures survive Obsidian being force-quit.

Building the Shortcut by hand

Only needed if the link fails or you want to know what it does. In Shortcuts, make a new shortcut named Capture Atom with these actions in order.

  1. Choose from Menu — two items, Type and Voice.
  2. Type branch: Ask for Input, prompt What's on your mind?, type Text.
  3. Type branch: Set Variable Capture to Provided Input.
  4. Voice branch: Dictate Text.
  5. Voice branch: Set Variable Capture to Dictated Text.
  6. Replace Text — find \n, replace with \n\t, Regular Expression on, input Capture.
  7. Format Date — Current Date, Date Format Custom, format string yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZZZZZ.
  8. Text — - then the formatted date, a space, then the replaced text. All one line.
  9. Append to Bookmark (Obsidian) — bookmark Atoms Inbox, Append, text from step 8.

Two traps, both of which cost real time when this was built on device. Set the format string on the Format Date action, not by tapping the blue Current Date chip — the chip's panel looks like the right place and changes nothing. And use ZZZZZ, not Z: a single Z writes -0400 where the parser needs -04:00. If your timestamps all say 12:00:00, the date variable got set to Date only — clear it and re-insert without picking a component.

Android

There is no Android equivalent yet, and we would rather say so than ship a recipe we have not run on a real device. The iOS version leans on a Shortcuts action that appends to an Obsidian bookmark; Android has no direct counterpart, so it needs a different design rather than a translation.

Until then, capture the plain way: open your daily note and type a top-level bullet. Atoms treats it identically — the Shortcut is a convenience, not a requirement, and nothing about the sorting depends on it.

3 · Ask

This is the part people set up last and then use most. Once it is on, you can ask Claude or ChatGPT about your own notes and get answers with citations back to the atoms they came from.

It is off until you turn it on, and it only ever sends your atoms folder — not your daily notes, and not the rest of your vault.

Turn on the mirror

In Settings → Atoms, switch on Enable Ask mirror and accept the summary it shows you. Your atoms are copied to the Atoms Plus service so an assistant can search them. The copy goes one direction only: nothing is ever written back over a note in your vault.

Add the connector

The same screen has an MCP connector URL with a Copy button. It is the same address for both assistants:

https://plus.tryatoms.app/mcp

  • Claude — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, then paste the URL.
  • ChatGPT — Settings → Apps & connectors, turn on Developer mode, add the URL, and complete the sign-in it prompts for.

Pair it

The connector's authorise page asks for a pairing code. Back in Settings → Atoms, press Get pairing code and paste what it gives you.

The code binds the connector to your Atoms Plus account, so the email on your Claude or ChatGPT account does not need to match. Codes expire quickly and are secrets — treat one like a password and do not paste it anywhere else.

Then just ask

Ask the way you would ask a person who had read everything: what have I said about sleep this year, or what did I think last time I tried this. Answers cite the atoms they came from, so you can open the note and read your own words in context.

There is an optional Allow filing from Claude or ChatGPT switch too. With it on, you can tell the assistant to remember something and it queues a new atom, which Obsidian writes into your vault the next time it syncs.

What goes where, in full, is on the Privacy page. Prefer to run the service yourself? The DIY guide is in the repository.
